reader.requirement: The Procedure Division may reference a Linkage Section item only if it is a USING operand of the header, subordinate to one, a REDEFINES or RENAMES whose object is one, subordinate to such a redefinition, or a condition-name or index-name of any of these; every other linkage reference is refused; and at least five USING operands are accepted in the header and the CALL.

refuses the BASED clause below 2002 (COBOL0900), so the BASED leg of SealLinkageRules is unreachable at 85

reader.notes: One per-record decision (SealLinkageRules) covers legs a-e: subordinates, RENAMES, condition-names and index-names follow their record, and a REDEFINES root follows its object. COBOL2746's text at --std 85 cites §2023:13.7.3 SR4 and suggests RETURNING or BASED, neither of which 1985 has: a wording point, not a conformance failure (the refusal is right).

refuter.evidence: Probe lk_odo.cob at --std 85 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-233/src; run lk_odo-001): callee LINKAGE 01 L1. 05 L1E PIC X OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING ON LN. 01 L2. 05 LN PIC 9. PROCEDURE DIVISION USING L1. DISPLAY "S L1=" L1 -- compiles clean and prints 'S L1=' (empty: LN, in the non-operand record L2, is read as 0 with no storage), though the caller passed 5 A's. 1985 defines a Procedure Division reference as explicit OR implicit: cite.py OK §1985:IV.4.4.1 the text is in the clause ('Such an implicit reference occurs if and only if the data item contributes to the execution of the statement'); LN contributes to DISPLAY L1 (it fixes L1's length), so LN is referenced within the Procedure Division, and GR4 admits that 'if, and only if' it satisfies a-e (cite.py OK §1985:X.5.1 GR4 the text is in GR4); LN satisfies none. 1985 OCCURS (§1985:VI SR1-12) puts no section restriction on data-name-1, so the source is otherwise legal and the reference is the only defect. Same output at --std 2023 (lk_odo-002). lk_callarg.cob: explicit references in a DECLARATIVES paragraph and as a CALL USING argument are refused COBOL2746 (the explicit path holds). kb/Work PB1249's sweep chose the opposite reading ('the data-division resolvers (OCCURS DEPENDING ...) are not within the procedure division and are not asked'), argued from the 2023 text; the 1985 text's IV.4.4.1 is the counter. The reader's probes covered only explicit references.

Harm: under-rejects / wrong-answer. Cause (b): the same at --std 2023. Reading stated: an implicit reference counts as 'referenced within the Procedure Division' (IV.4.4.1); under PB1249's reading (only written references) the verdict stays CONFORMS. adjudication.reason: A Linkage item that is not addressable (the DEPENDING ON object of a USING operand's table, in a record that is no operand) is referenced implicitly by every statement that references the table's record, which the rule forbids; the program compiles and reads no storage (lk_odo.cob: S L1= prints empty).
